The last common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*) is the last common ancestor of **all placental mammals** (Eutheria).  
This ancestor lived roughly 100–110 million years ago, during the early Cretaceous, before the major placental lineages (including the carnivores and the odd‑toed ungulates) split off from one another.
